labels.label: rem:intuitively_spread_thinner_than
labels.notes: GX.intuitively_spread_thinner_of_local takes exactly spread_top_of_local's hypotheses (DEC-87(d)) and proves IsGreatest {σ' | σ' ≤ T_{M̃^S} ∧ IsSpread σ' T p} (p^*T). In mathlib's order that says p^*T is the coarsest spread topology among those finer than the natural one. GX.IsSpread (GX/Spread/Basic.lean:136) is continuity plus generation by components of preimages, so it is the paper's notion and not a trivialised one. The restriction σ' ≤ T_M is needed even inside the setting. Example: a non-injective covering p with T = T_N, where σ' = p⁻¹T_N is a spread strictly coarser than T_M. The restriction is in the decl named by WP-40d's ruling question (accepted, DEC-87), and its provenance is now stated in REPORT. The 'However' sentence is a negative claim about the definition in general. GX.cex_component_not_strongPull_connected witnesses it with p = id on ℝ (a spread), T = cutTopReal ≤ usual (proved), and ℝ, the usual component, not p^*T-preconnected. Two counterexamples to the unrestricted reading are kept and disclosed (SCOPE (f)).

labels.label: rem:hypothesis_model_spaces_necessary
labels.notes: Read under DEC-87(b). GX.hypothesis_model_spaces_necessary covers every α > 0 with α ≠ 2π, the paper's θ ∈ ℝ₊∖{0,2π}. Its subject is MassCyl α with G = Isom₀. Its structure hypothesis IsMassiveStructure is satisfiable (exists_isMassiveStructure, axioms clean). The decl proves seven things: (1) sing = the axis; (2) the model is tame ('(B) certainly satisfied'); (3) Φ : M̃ ≃ₜ 𝔻_∞×ℝ over E_α; (4) the natural topology and the transported BTZ topology btzGenTop (natural ⊓ generateFrom {rθ²<λ}, l.1953) are tamifying; (5) T' = mixedTop(T, {t>0}) is literally 'generated by the natural one and T|{t>0}'; (6) T' is tamifying, which includes (C), the Galois group preserving T', and makes the remark's unproved claim a theorem; (7) the time shift by 2 lies in aeAutMapsMax, the a.e.-automorphism homeomorphisms of M̃ (Models:1455, i.e. Aut(X̃_α)), is T-continuous and is not T'-continuous. IsTamifyingTopology (Models:1467) carries ≤ natural, FC, LPC and (A)-(D), so it is not trivialised. The sentence 'the proof fails since T_{U,V,φ} depends on V' is a claim about theo:local_virt_tame's proof. SCOPE (c) discloses this, and the abstract mechanism is GX.hypothesis_model_spaces_mechanism. The final sentence is the author's open question. Neither carries an owed assertion.

labels.label: rem:quotient_virtually_tame
labels.notes: Read under DEC-87(c): N Galoisian, isomorphic = homeomorphic. GX.quotient_virtually_tame_galoisian' takes any tamifying T (at least 'M virtually tame') and any Galoisian N possibly branched over sing M. N is T2/LPC/FC (DEC-66) and M carries the standing hypotheses, with hSc the presupposition of M̃. It produces the universal Pj : M̃ → N (maxBranched_universal). Then, for every injective D continuous for coinduced Pj T and with holonomy ρ, it gives Quotient(orbit setoid of ρ on range D) ≃ₜ M, sending [D n] to π_N n, with D(N) carrying devImageTop = induced(X) ⊓ generateFrom{D-images of Pj_*T-opens}. That matches the three items. The paper's hypothesis, 'D a developing map' (def:developing_map: an a.e. (G,X)-morphism), implies the decl's. It is continuous for the natural topology of N, which is coarser than Pj_*T. It has a holonomy by GX.holonomyOf_spec / existsUnique_holonomyOf (strict GX/SingularII/Developing.lean). So the decl is at least as strong as the remark. The hypotheses are satisfiable: N = M̃.
